VERDICT: CHANGES REQUESTED

The household refactor itself is well-factored: `deriveHouseholdId`, `findHouseholdMembers`, `rejectWhenHouseholdDuplicate`, and `assignPossibleDuplicate` are each cohesive, the create-flow step sequence in `createOwner` reads cleanly, and the javadocs were faithfully rewritten to match the new behaviour. `AddressNormalizer`/`IdentityKeyNormalizer` are correctly dropped from the imports and remain used elsewhere (OwnerMapper, the V1 controller), so nothing is orphaned.

One structural issue:

- **Duplicated SHA-256 hex helper** (`ClinicServiceImpl.java:458` and `:477`). The new `sha256HexPrefix(value, hexChars)` is a near-copy of the existing `sha256Hex8(value)`: same `MessageDigest.getInstance("SHA-256")`, same UTF-8 digest, same byte→hex `StringBuilder` loop, same `NoSuchAlgorithmException`→`IllegalStateException` handling. The only real differences are the length (fixed 8 vs. parameterized) and the case (`%02X` upper vs. `%02x` lower). Having two parallel digest-to-hex helpers side by side is exactly the kind of duplication a maintainer of this class would flag, and it will drift the next time someone touches one. Consolidate: keep the general `sha256HexPrefix(value, hexChars)` (lower-case) as the single primitive and express the customer-code helper in terms of it, e.g. `sha256Hex8(value)` → `sha256HexPrefix(value, 8).toUpperCase()`. If the upper/lower distinction should be first-class, make a single `sha256HexPrefix(value, hexChars, upperCase)` and have both call sites use it.

Minor (not blocking): `assignPossibleDuplicate` has collapsed to two unconditional setters. It still earns its place via the explanatory javadoc and the uniform step-per-method shape of `createOwner`, so keeping it is defensible — just noting it now sits close to the line of being inlineable.
